summary: Server-side advisor-only enforcement verified end-to-end. 31/31 pytest cases PASS in new /app/backend/tests/test_role_enforcement.py. Covered all 7 advisor GET endpoints (clients, reports, emails, compliance, portfolio-review, smart-suggestions/all, client-360/{id}), all 5 advisor POST endpoints (POST /clients, /reports/generate, /emails/generate, /compliance/generate, /portfolio-review/generate), 4 shared endpoints (documents/analyses, me/financial/profile|dashboard|history), unauthenticated requests, and a freshly-registered no-role user. Individual → 403 with exact detail 'This endpoint is for financial advisors only.'; Advisor → 200; missing token → 401/403 (and detail is NEVER the advisor-only one, proving the dependency ordering is right — auth check fires before role check). Shared endpoints continue to return 200 for individuals — no regression.
critical_code_review_comments: require_advisor in /app/backend/utils/auth.py:106-118 — clean implementation: admin bypass first, then role=='advisor', else 403 with the exact spec'd detail message. Good.

Import alias trick `from utils.auth import require_advisor as get_current_user` in all 7 advisor route files is elegant — zero per-endpoint changes required. Verified all 7 files have the import (client_360, clients, compliance, emails, portfolio_review, reports, smart_suggestions).

However, this aliasing means the local variable bound to the dependency result is now the FULL user dict from get_current_user (returned by require_advisor) rather than the previously-imported get_current_user. Spot-checked behaviour is unchanged because the inner get_current_user already returns the full user dict, so existing code paths inside the routes that use current_user['id'] / current_user.get('advisor_id') keep working — consistent with the green test suite.

401 vs 403 ordering is correct: missing/invalid token raises HTTPBearer/decode_token 401 BEFORE require_advisor runs, so unauth requests do NOT receive the advisor-only detail message (asserted explicitly in test_unauthenticated_gets_401_or_403).

Shared routes (documents.py, my_money.py) correctly were NOT touched — they still expose get_current_user from utils.auth without the advisor guard, confirmed by individual-user 200s on /api/documents/analyses, /api/me/financial/profile|dashboard|history.
No-role user (newly registered, no role set in payload) gets 403 — the default role-less account is treated as non-advisor as expected. Server's auth/register defaults role correctly.

Minor suggestion (non-blocking): the import alias couples two distinct concerns at the import site. A clearer long-term pattern would be an explicit router-level `dependencies=[Depends(require_advisor)]` on the APIRouter — but the current alias trick is contained and works.
